extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners and parties participating in PTAB inter partes review (IPR) proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for evaluating whether a petitioner has shown motivation to combine prior art references and related obviousness inquiries in an inter partes review, including treatment of expert testimony, burdens of proof, and secondary considerations (objective indicia) nexus analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motivation to combine prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitioner must articulate an adequate motivation to combine the teachings of the prior art to arrive at the claimed invention; mere statements that references relate to the same field are insufficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board requires a satisfactory explanation of 'how the combination of the . . . references [is] supposed to work' to support a conclusion that a skilled artisan would be motivated to make the combination and reasonably expect success. Short-cut logic that references are in the same field is not enough. The Board weighs putative benefits against drawbacks to determine whether there would have been a motivation to combine (citing Personal Web Techs., Trivascular, Arctic Cat, Securus, Comcast).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable expectation of success
rubrics_metrics.description: A petitioner must show that a person of ordinary skill in the art would have had a reasonable expectation of success in combining the teachings of the references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is not sufficient to assert potential improvements; the petitioner must provide evidence or reasoning that the substituted/combined elements would be expected to achieve the claimed result in the relevant context (see discussion of Petitioner’s claim that Huang's calculation could replace Kim's flatness examination).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cannot rely on a generic desire to 'build something better'
rubrics_metrics.description: A generic desire to improve or that one reference 'obtains better image quality' is insufficient standing alone to show motivation to combine prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite ActiveVideo Networks v. Verizon and related authority: evidence must connect the asserted improvement to the specific features the petitioner relies on, not just a general superiority claim. Petitioner retains the burden to prove the claimed advantage of the combination when that is the theory of motivation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analogy/field-of-art is not determinative
rubrics_metrics.description: The mere fact that references are directed to the same art or address similar technical issues cannot alone establish a motivation to combine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While related-field proximity is a factor, it cannot by itself substitute for a reasoned rationale; petitioner must show more than that the references come from the same field (see Microsoft v. Enfish, Comcast, Securus).

rubrics_metrics.name: Explanation of how the combination would work (no 'bodily incorporation' required but must explain operation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Although physical or bodily incorporation of a reference is not required, petitioner must provide a satisfactory explanation of how the combination is supposed to work and how the elements would be implemented together.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Citing Personal Web Techs., Trivascular, petitioner must explain how and why the modification or substitution would be made and how it would operate in the combined system; conclusory statements are insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden of persuasion on petitioner
rubrics_metrics.description: The petitioner bears the burden to prove unpatentability by a preponderance of the evidence under 35 U.S.C. § 316(e); that burden never shifts to the patentee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitioner must meet its evidentiary burden for motivation to combine and reasonable expectation of success; failures cannot be remedied by shifting burdens to Patent Owner (citing Dynamic Drinkware, Magnum Oil).

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden of production does not shift to patentee on motivation/obviousness
rubrics_metrics.description: No burden shifts from the patent challenger to the patentee where the only issues are motivation to combine and whether that combination would render the claims obvious.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even with patentees presenting evidence, the petitioner's ultimate burden remains unchanged (Magnum Oil Tools).

rubrics_metrics.name: Expert testimony must provide reasoned analysis and evidentiary linkage
rubrics_metrics.description: Expert testimony that merely states conclusions without linking evidence in the record or prior art statements to those conclusions is inadequate to show motivation or expectation of success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts have reversed findings based on expert testimony that fails to provide meaningful explanation for why a skilled artisan would combine references (TQ Delta, InTouch, DSS Tech Mgmt.). Cross-examined experts with no opinion on key factual applicability are weak support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attorney arguments cannot substitute for evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Arguments of counsel cannot take the place of evidence lacking in the record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unsupported attorney argument is insufficient; the record must contain testimony, demonstrative evidence, or prior art statements to support claimed rationales (Estee Lauder, In re Pearson).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness of arguments — new theories in reply may be disregarded
rubrics_metrics.description: Arguments raised for the first time in a reply brief that were not presented in the petition may be untimely and need not be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board need not consider new, belated arguments in a reply (Intelligent Bio-Systems, Acceleration Bay).

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparisons must be between relevant types of art (context matters)
rubrics_metrics.description: An asserted superiority in one context (e.g., still-image deblocking) does not automatically translate to superiority in a different context (e.g., real-time video deblocking).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitioner must show the prior-art comparison is to appropriate, comparable techniques; Huang’s claims about still-image performance could not be assumed to apply to video without supporting evidence. Consider practical differences like real-time constraints and edge-map reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Need to show asserted improvement is attributable to the relied-upon feature
rubrics_metrics.description: If a reference claims an overall improvement, a petitioner relying on only one feature of that reference must show that the improvement is attributable to that specific feature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board requires evidence linking the claimed benefit to the particular element the petitioner substitutes (e.g., show Huang's classification, not just its nonlinear filter, causes improvement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Weigh benefits against drawbacks (practical tradeoffs)
rubrics_metrics.description: When assessing motivation to combine, the Board weighs putative benefits of the modification against its drawbacks (e.g., computational cost, incompatibility with goals like real-time processing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrated practical disadvantages (e.g., two orders of magnitude slower, unsuitable for real-time) can negate a claimed motivation to combine (citing Arctic Cat).

rubrics_metrics.name: Obviousness requires selection/combination as part of ordinary research and development
rubrics_metrics.description: Obviousness requires showing that a person of ordinary skill would have selected and combined prior art elements in the normal course of research and development to yield the claimed invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Piecemeal combination of portions of different methods requires showing that such piecemeal combination would have been part of normal research activities (KSR, Unigene Labs).

rubrics_metrics.name: No justification from mere later publication date
rubrics_metrics.description: The fact that one reference was published later than another does not, by itself, provide a basis to conclude it would have been viewed as superior or would motivate substitution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expert testimony relying solely on later publication timing is insufficient; need substantive technical linkage and rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective indicia (secondary considerations) enumerated
rubrics_metrics.description: Objective indicia of nonobviousness may include long-felt but unsolved need, failure of others, unexpected results, commercial success, copying, licensing, industry praise, and expert skepticism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These factors are relevant only if there is a nexus between the claimed invention and the indicia; the Board will consider these for completeness even if primary rationale fails, but nexus is required (Mintz, Affinity Labs, Fox Factory).

rubrics_metrics.name: Nexus requirement and coextensiveness presumption
rubrics_metrics.description: Objective indicia are relevant only if there is a nexus between the claimed invention and the evidence; a patentee may get a rebuttable presumption of nexus by showing its products are coextensive with the challenged claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board uses a two-step analysis: (1) determine if patentee's products are coextensive with the claims (presumption of nexus), and (2) if not coextensive, patentee can still prove nexus by showing the evidence is the direct result of unique claimed characteristics (Lectrosonics, Fox Factory).

rubrics_metrics.name: Once prima facie nexus established, challenger must rebut
rubrics_metrics.description: If the patentee presents a prima facie case of nexus, the burden of coming forward with rebuttal evidence shifts to the challenger to show the objective indicia were due to extraneous factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite Demaco: after patent owner shows nexus, challenger must adduce evidence that factors other than the patented invention explain the indicia.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board may revise its preliminary view after development of record
rubrics_metrics.description: An institution decision based on a preliminary record can be revised after a fuller trial record is developed; the Board may change its view if convinced initial inclinations were wrong.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite Trivascular: Board is free to change its view after further development of the record and should do so if convinced its initial inclination was wrong.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims or limitations unsupported by petitioner may be deemed waived
rubrics_metrics.description: If Patent Owner does not respond to petitioner's arguments directed to particular claim limitations, the Board may find those arguments waived and accept the petitioner's showing for those limitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where Patent Owner does not specifically respond, the Board may treat arguments as waived (see examples where Patent Owner did not respond to arguments for certain limitations and Board found them satisfied).
